paper: DCdetector: Dual Attention Contrastive Representation Learning for Time Series Anomaly Detection

paper: TimeSeriesBench: An Industrial-Grade Benchmark for Time Series Anomaly Detection Models

caveat: Software-system time series and preprint status; not a direct FD002 comparison.

paper: TSB-UAD: An End-to-End Benchmark Suite for Univariate Time-Series Anomaly Detection
model: Standardizes many datasets and methods in a reproducible end-to-end benchmark.
caveat: Univariate benchmark; FD002 is multivariate and engine-grouped.

paper: TimeEval: A Benchmarking Toolkit for Time Series Anomaly Detection Algorithms
model: Provides an extensible automated framework for comparable detector, dataset, runtime, and metric experiments.
caveat: A toolkit does not solve FD002 label ambiguity or define engine-level operational metrics.

paper: Evaluating Real-time Anomaly Detection Algorithms: The Numenta Anomaly Benchmark
model: Defines time-sensitive anomaly windows and rewards early detection while penalizing false positives.
caveat: Univariate streaming benchmark and application-weighted score are not directly transferable.

paper: Local Evaluation of Time Series Anomaly Detection Algorithms
model: Introduces affiliation precision/recall using distances between predicted and true event sets with local interpretation.
caveat: Still requires meaningful labeled event ranges, which FD002 does not provide directly.

paper: PATE: Proximity-Aware Time Series Anomaly Evaluation
model: Weights early and delayed detections using buffer zones and provides proximity-aware area under precision-recall.
caveat: Parameters and interval semantics must be fixed before seeing test results.

paper: Do You Know Existing Accuracy Metrics Overrate Time-Series Anomaly Detections?
model: Shows common range and point-adjusted metrics can overrate imprecise detections; proposes enhanced temporal precision/recall.
caveat: No metric removes the need to define the operational meaning of an event.

paper: Position: Quo Vadis, Unsupervised Time Series Anomaly Detection?
model: Critiques flawed metrics, inconsistent benchmark practices, and weak justification for deep architectural complexity.
caveat: Position paper rather than a detector benchmark; conclusions should guide protocol, not replace evidence.

paper: Optimal Detection of Changepoints With a Linear Computational Cost
model: Introduces PELT, an exact penalized segmentation algorithm with linear expected cost under stated conditions.
caveat: Offline segmentation gives an estimated statistical change, not physical degradation ground truth.

paper: Bayesian Online Changepoint Detection
model: Maintains a posterior over run length to infer the most recent generative-parameter change online.
caveat: Requires a predictive model and hazard prior; estimated change remains model-dependent.

paper: Selective Review of Offline Change Point Detection Methods
model: Organizes methods by cost function, search, and constraint; links theory to the ruptures implementation.
caveat: A broad review; method selection and calibration remain application-specific.

paper: Change-Point Detection in Time-Series Data by Relative Density-Ratio Estimation
model: Estimates relative Pearson divergence directly between neighboring windows without separately estimating densities.
caveat: Window and regularization choices affect onset; not a true FD002 label.

paper: Kernel Change-Point Detection
model: Uses kernel representations and model selection to find distributional changes beyond mean shifts.
caveat: Computational and kernel-selection sensitivity; estimated changes are not physical labels.

paper: Control Chart Tests Based on Geometric Moving Averages
model: Foundational exponentially/geometrically weighted moving-average monitoring for small process shifts.
caveat: Classical assumptions do not automatically hold for autocorrelated learned anomaly scores.

paper: Continuous Inspection Schemes
model: Introduces cumulative-sum inspection logic for persistent sequential shifts.
caveat: CUSUM requires a declared in-control distribution and tuning for score dependence.

paper: Learning from Time-Changing Data with Adaptive Windowing
model: ADWIN adapts the window length from statistically detected changes rather than a fixed update horizon.
caveat: Blind adaptation can still learn degradation; detector updates need a healthy-state gate.

paper: A Survey on Concept Drift Adaptation
model: Taxonomizes drift detection, adaptation strategies, evaluation, and application settings.
caveat: Concept drift is not identical to irreversible degradation and supervised framing often differs.

paper: Why Should I Trust You?: Explaining the Predictions of Any Classifier
model: Introduces LIME, fitting an interpretable local surrogate around an individual prediction.
caveat: Local surrogate fidelity and perturbation design are crucial, especially for correlated sequences.

paper: Axiomatic Attribution for Deep Networks
model: Introduces Integrated Gradients using sensitivity and implementation-invariance axioms.
caveat: Attributions depend on the baseline and explain a scalar model output, not necessarily a causal fault.

paper: Learning Important Features Through Propagating Activation Differences
model: DeepLIFT decomposes output differences from a reference activation into feature contributions.
caveat: Reference choice and network operation rules affect interpretation.

paper: TimeSHAP: Explaining Recurrent Models through Sequence Perturbations
model: Extends KernelSHAP to feature-, event-, and cell-level attributions with sequence pruning.
caveat: Computational cost, perturbation realism, and correlated sensor-time inputs can weaken fidelity.

paper: Explaining Anomalies Detected by Autoencoders Using SHAP
model: Uses KernelSHAP around an autoencoder anomaly score to show features increasing or offsetting anomalousness.
caveat: Perturbations and surrogate fidelity must be validated; explanations are not root-cause proof.

paper: Feature Bagging for Outlier Detection
model: Combines outlier detectors trained on random feature subsets to improve robustness in noisy high dimensions.
caveat: Random sensor subsets may destroy important temporal/physical dependencies.

paper: LSCP: Locally Selective Combination in Parallel Outlier Ensembles
model: Selects locally competent base outlier detectors before combining their scores.
caveat: Competence estimation without ground truth adds complexity and possible overfitting.

paper: SUOD: Accelerating Large-Scale Unsupervised Heterogeneous Outlier Detection
model: Accelerates many heterogeneous detectors using data reduction, model approximation, and balanced scheduling.
caveat: An acceleration system does not establish that an ensemble improves scientific validity.

paper: Interpreting and Unifying Outlier Scores
model: Maps heterogeneous arbitrary outlier factors to a common interpretable range before comparison or combination.
caveat: Probability-like normalization is model-based and not guaranteed to be calibrated probability.

paper: Explainable Deep One-Class Classification
model: FCDD makes a fully convolutional one-class output map serve directly as an anomaly explanation map.
caveat: Image-specific architecture; not directly applicable to 30-by-21 sensor sequences.

paper: On the Evaluation of Unsupervised Outlier Detection: Measures, Datasets, and an Empirical Study
model: Studies evaluation measures, benchmark construction, contamination, and instability across many outlier detectors.
caveat: Mostly tabular outlier settings; temporal grouping and early warning require additional metrics.
